title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Tech stocks slumped Friday as chip and data-center names sold off ahead of Nvidia's Tuesday earnings; Nasdaq fell 0.9%, S&P 500 fell 0.4%, Dow rose 0.1%, and Nvidia closed down 2% after giving up early gains.

Markets: Treasury yields rose sharply on hardening bets for further Fed rate hikes (10-year near 5.15%) before a Friday selloff pause; oil ticked up on Mideast conflict concerns, while gold and bitcoin softened.

Companies: Nvidia's board confirmed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and director Harvey Jones as its first-ever board chair following Jensen Huang's resignation; the search for a permanent successor is underway.

Companies: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei said he hopes the IPO will 'underpromise and overdeliver,' with the company still targeting a roughly $1.33T valuation and shares expected to begin trading next Thursday.
Companies: Microsoft shares recovered to little changed after a widespread Teams/Outlook outage; chipmaker Cerebras beat Q3 revenue estimates, raised its forecast, and announced a new Microsoft deal.

Macro/Policy: October wholesale prices (PPI) rose 0.3% m/m, cooling from September, but the 12-month rate climbed to 6.5% from 6.3%, reinforcing a hawkish Fed tilt; Congress (Sens. Warren, Kennedy) is pressing Commerce Secretary Lutnick over delayed chip-export-control action tied to the Huang scandal, while the White House continues to back him.
